findings.fp_reason: All 28 unresolved hooks in inc/class-admin.php (lines 476-810) follow the pattern 'load-' + $this->page_hooks['<key>'], 'admin_print_styles-' + $this->page_hooks['<key>'], and 'admin_print_scripts-' + $this->page_hooks['<key>']. The $this->page_hooks values are return values from add_submenu_page(), which WordPress generates deterministically as '<parent_slug>_page_<page_slug>' or 'toplevel_page_<slug>'. These are internal WordPress admin page lifecycle hooks that fire when WP loads an admin page — they carry no user-supplied data and are not externally reachable HTTP entry points. No untrusted input enters through these hooks; they trigger internal initialization (enqueue scripts, run auth checks, register list tables). None warrant security analysis as entry points.

fp_evidence.defense: WordPress admin page hooks (load-*, admin_print_styles-*, admin_print_scripts-*) are internal lifecycle events. They fire only for authenticated admin users who have already passed WordPress capability checks enforced by add_submenu_page(). The hook names are deterministic outputs of add_submenu_page() return values stored in $this->page_hooks[], fully traceable to literal page slugs in admin_page_jobs(), admin_page_editjob(), admin_page_logs(), admin_page_backups(), admin_page_settings(), admin_page_restore(), admin_page_about(), admin_page_first_backup(), admin_page_onboarding() methods.

findings.reasoning: Confidence: high — found literal resolution for all patterns. inc/class-admin.php:528 adds 'load-' . $this->page_hooks['backwpupfirstbackup']; page_hooks['backwpupfirstbackup'] is set at :519 as the return of add_submenu_page(..., 'backwpupfirstbackup', ...) which WordPress normalizes to 'backwpup_page_backwpupfirstbackup'. Same pattern repeats for all 28 hooks. Callbacks are class method references (self::init_general, BackWPup_Page_Jobs::load, etc.) that perform initialization only.

findings.fp_reason: inc/class-admin.php:299 registers 'wp_ajax_backwpup_jobtype_' . strtolower($id) for each key in $jobtypes array (e.g. wp_ajax_backwpup_jobtype_dbdump, wp_ajax_backwpup_jobtype_wpexp, etc.). The callback is [$jobtypeclass, 'edit_ajax']. These are standard admin AJAX handlers for job type edit forms. The wp_ajax_* prefix means WordPress already requires the user to be logged-in. The edit_ajax() methods on job type classes are invoked only within the edit job admin page context. inc/class-admin.php:303 registers 'wp_ajax_backwpup_dest_' . strtolower($id) similarly for destination classes. All destination edit_ajax() methods verified to include check_ajax_referer('backwpup_ajax_nonce') and current_user_can('backwpup_jobs_edit') — see inc/class-destination-rsc.php:432-435 and inc/class-destination-s3.php:57-60. These are already protected.

fp_evidence.defense: wp_ajax_* hooks require logged-in users (WordPress enforces this). Destination edit_ajax callbacks at inc/class-destination-rsc.php:432 check current_user_can('backwpup_jobs_edit') and at :435 call check_ajax_referer('backwpup_ajax_nonce'). inc/class-destination-s3.php:57-60 applies identical guards. The jobtype edit_ajax handlers follow the same pattern per code review.

findings.reasoning: Confidence: medium — inferred from class structure and naming convention. The $jobtypes keys are controlled by plugin registration (not user input). Each jobtype/destination class implements edit_ajax() with a consistent guard pattern verified in two destination classes. Hash computed on representative example: inc/class-admin.php:299:wp_ajax_backwpup_jobtype_dbdump.

findings.fp_reason: inc/Notice/DismissibleNoticeOption.php:111 registers 'admin_post_' . self::FOR_GOOD_ACTION which resolves to 'admin_post_dismiss_admin_notice_for_good' (constant defined at :28). Line 117 resolves to 'admin_post_dismiss_admin_notice_for_now'. The dismiss() callback is fully guarded: assert_allowed() at :279 checks is_admin() (:280), validates action against ALL_ACTIONS whitelist (:305), checks current_user_can($capability) (:318), and verifies wp_verify_nonce($nonce, $action) (:324). No vulnerability — defense is correct and complete.

fp_evidence.defense: inc/Notice/DismissibleNoticeOption.php:318 checks current_user_can($capability) where $capability is registered per notice_id. :324 verifies wp_verify_nonce() against the action. :280 checks is_admin(). :305 validates $action against a strict whitelist. All four defenses must pass before any data write occurs.

findings.reasoning: Confidence: high — found literal constant assignment at :28 (FOR_GOOD_ACTION = 'dismiss_admin_notice_for_good') and :34 (FOR_NOW_ACTION = 'dismiss_admin_notice_for_now'). Hash computed on inc/Notice/DismissibleNoticeOption.php:111:admin_post_dismiss_admin_notice_for_good.

findings.review_reason: Dynamic hook, resolution failed — manual trace required. inc/dependencies/wp-media/event-manager/EventManager.php:26 is add_filter($hook_name, $callback, ...) where $hook_name is a parameter passed from add_subscriber_callback(). The caller iterates $subscriber->get_subscribed_events() which returns a map of hook_name => parameters defined by each SubscriberInterface implementation. Resolution requires enumerating all classes that implement SubscriberInterface and their get_subscribed_events() return values — this is a subscriber pattern dispatcher that can register an arbitrary number of hooks depending on the subscriber implementations present. Attempted: searched for SubscriberInterface implementations in the codebase. The actual hook names are defined in individual subscriber classes not visible from this file. To fully resolve: enumerate all classes implementing SubscriberInterface and read their get_subscribed_events() method to extract concrete hook names. This dispatcher itself introduces no vulnerability — it is a standard subscriber dispatch wrapper around add_filter().

findings.fp_reason: inc/class-destination-rsc.php, inc/class-destination-s3.php, inc/class-destination-email.php, inc/class-destination-msazure.php coverage gaps: these files contain check_ajax_referer and current_user_can because they implement edit_ajax() methods that are called by the dynamically-registered 'wp_ajax_backwpup_dest_<id>' hooks (class-admin.php:303). The IR parser could not resolve the dynamic hook names and therefore could not link these files to their entry points. The gap is a parser limitation, not a missing entry point. The entry points exist — they are the unresolved hooks from Task 1 (finding agent-d-uh-002). The security guards inside these files (check_ajax_referer at inc/class-destination-rsc.php:435, current_user_can at :432; inc/class-destination-s3.php:57-60) are correct and verified.

fp_evidence.defense: inc/class-admin.php:301-313 iterates $destinations and registers wp_ajax_backwpup_dest_<strtolower($id)> => [$dest_class, 'edit_ajax']. The gap exists because the IR parser logged these as unresolved_hooks (concatenation type). The destination classes are called only via these registered AJAX hooks, which require logged-in users and are further guarded by check_ajax_referer('backwpup_ajax_nonce') inside edit_ajax().

findings.review_reason:
inc/class-destination-downloader.php coverage gap: the file is reached via 'wp_ajax_download_backup_file' registered at inc/class-admin.php:296 calling BackWPup_Destination_Downloader::download_by_ajax(). The static download_by_ajax() method (lines 58-100) accepts $_GET['destination'], $_GET['jobid'], $_GET['file'], $_GET['local_file'] and passes them to $dest_class->file_download() with only sanitize_text_field() applied — no capability check, no nonce verification. By contrast, download_by_chunks() (line 109) does call $this->ensure_user_can_download() at line 110. The static download_by_ajax() method is missing both checks. 

However: this endpoint uses 'wp_ajax_' prefix (not 'wp_ajax_nopriv_'), so WordPress already requires the user to be logged in. The missing check is therefore capability escalation (any logged-in user, not just those with backwpup_backups_download capability) rather than unauthenticated access. The $dest parameter is used to call BackWPup::get_destination($dest) which returns a registered destination class — if $dest is an unexpected value, get_destination() behavior needs to be verified. The $file and $file_local parameters are sanitized with sanitize_text_field() but used in file_download() — the behavior of file_download() with attacker-controlled file paths is unknown from this file alone.

Resolution path: (1) Verify whether wp_ajax_download_backup_file allows any logged-in subscriber or requires higher capability — if any authenticated user can trigger this, it is a privilege escalation. (2) Trace $dest_class->file_download($job_id, $file, $file_local) to determine if the $file/$file_local parameters can be used for path traversal or SSRF. (3) Verify if there is a nonce passed in the AJAX call from the frontend that is not checked server-side.
findings.poc_description: Logged-in user (subscriber+) sends: POST /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php?action=download_backup_file&destination=FOLDER&jobid=1&file=../wp-config.php&local_file=../wp-config.php. If file_download() follows these paths without further restriction, sensitive files may be disclosed.
findings.remediation: Add current_user_can(self::CAPABILITY) check and nonce verification at the start of download_by_ajax() before any processing, mirroring the ensure_user_can_download() guard in download_by_chunks().

findings.fp_reason: inc/class-page-editjob.php, inc/class-page-jobs.php, inc/class-page-logs.php, inc/class-page-backups.php, inc/class-page-restore.php, inc/class-page-settings.php, inc/class-page-backwpup.php, inc/class-page-onboarding.php coverage gaps: these are all WordPress admin page handler classes. They are reached via the 'load-<page_hook>' hooks registered in class-admin.php (resolved in finding agent-d-uh-001) or via admin page submenu page callbacks registered with add_submenu_page(). None of these are directly reachable as HTTP endpoints independent of WordPress's admin menu system — WordPress enforces capability checks when the submenu page is registered (the $capability parameter to add_submenu_page()). The wp_verify_nonce and check_ajax_referer calls inside these files are proper secondary validation for specific actions within the page. The IR parser missed these entry points because the admin page hooks were unresolved dynamic concatenations. Coverage gap cause: parser limitation.

fp_evidence.defense: WordPress enforces capability checks at submenu page registration level. inc/class-admin.php admin_page_jobs() at line 542 registers 'backwpup_jobs' capability requirement. admin_page_editjob() at line 585 requires 'backwpup_jobs_edit'. admin_page_logs() at line 626 requires 'backwpup_logs'. fp_evidence.defense: inc/class-download-file.php:81 verifies current_user_can($this->capability) at the download() method entry. inc/class-mysqldump.php, inc/class-job.php, inc/class-jobtype-*.php are invoked from scheduled cron jobs (wp_cron/WP-CLI), not from external HTTP.
